usefulness.example: A company runs 500 candidate submissions for an 'add two integers safely' task. The agent ranks them by correctness, edge-case handling and memory safety, and gives an explainable per-metric score.
usefulness.benefit: Fast first-round filtering where every rejection can be justified metric by metric.

usefulness.use_case: Plagiarism and LLM-copy triage for instructors
usefulness.example: Two submissions reach a similarity of 0.93 against the 0.85 threshold, so the agent raises a flag in the report. The instructor reviews only those pairs instead of all 300.
usefulness.benefit: Saves review time by narrowing manual checking to suspicious cases.

usefulness.use_case: Automated continuous formative feedback in programming labs
usefulness.example: Students submit code iteratively during a weekly lab; the agent instantly returns failing counter-examples, memory safety alerts (ASan), and style advice before final grading.
usefulness.benefit: Accelerates student learning loops and drastically reduces TA grading workload.

usefulness.use_case: Security and sanity gating for low-level systems codebases
usefulness.example: A CI/CD pipeline runs the agent on PR submissions to verify no undefined behavior (signed integer overflow, buffer overflows) or infinite loops enter the codebase.
usefulness.benefit: Enforces strict memory safety and C standards compliance in automated deployment.

limitations.limitation: Tests cannot prove correctness (Incomplete input space)
limitations.example: A submission passes all 10 hidden tests but fails when input has extra leading whitespace or an unconventional newline format not represented in the suite. The agent mistakenly awards 10/10 correctness.
limitations.mitigation: The agent should create adversarial LLM test inputs and compare student answers with a verified reference oracle.

limitations.limitation: Static structure and modularity heuristics can be easily gamed
limitations.example: A student inflates modularity from 3/10 to 10/10 by creating trivial unused helper functions (e.g., 'int unused() { return 0; }') without improving the true architecture of main().
limitations.mitigation: Use abstract syntax tree (AST) call-graph analysis to verify helper functions are actively called and contribute to computation.

limitations.limitation: Empirical complexity estimation is susceptible to OS scheduling noise
limitations.example: Under heavy CPU load or virtualization jitter on a shared server, an O(1) constant-time program exhibits runtime variance across test sizes, causing the estimator to falsely flag it as O(N).
limitations.mitigation: Measure hardware performance counters (such as CPU instruction retirement via perf or cachegrind) instead of wall-clock time.

limitations.limitation: Plagiarism false positives on short, constrained problems
limitations.example: For simple problems like 'add two integers', all correct solutions naturally share 85-95% structural and token similarity, triggering false plagiarism alarms on innocent submissions.
limitations.mitigation: Combine token diffing with Control Flow Graph (CFG) isomorphic subgraph matching and ignore standard boilerplate.
